projects.name: Plant Care Assistant
steps: Wire the soil probe and BME280, flash the starter sketch, confirm Serial output.
Calibrate dry and wet points and store them on the backend.
Deploy the backend, register the device token, confirm POST /api/readings returns 201.
Build the Plant screen with the moisture chart and threshold bands.
Run a 48 h soak across one watering cycle and compare advice with the drying curve.

criteria.text: Readings every 5 min ± 30 s, at least 95% delivered over 48 h.
Soil % moves at least 30 points from dry to freshly watered, and stays within ±5 points over 1 h idle.
AI report is valid JSON in 10 of 10 calls, cites a metric, and includes an uncertainty.
A synthetic disconnected probe (raw 0 or 4095) returns a data-quality warning and no watering advice.
No code path from AI output to GPIO or an actuator.

projects.name: Room Environment Monitor
steps: Reuse BME280 data. Add Room charts and comfort bands (about 20–26 °C, 40–60% RH).
Extend /api/summary with daily min, max, mean and 3 h pressure tendency.
Add project=room and a daily summary button. Phase 2 schedules it at 21:00 IST.
Compare the BME280 with a reference thermometer and hygrometer for 24 h.

criteria.text: After the vented enclosure fix, temperature is within ±1.0 °C and humidity within ±5% RH of the reference.
Daily summary covers all three metrics, flags comfort-band breaks longer than 2 h, and lists data gaps.
Summary returns in under 10 s and is served from cache on a repeat click within 30 min.

projects.name: Home Event Assistant
steps: Wire PIR to GPIO27, retrigger H, time pot minimum (~3 s), sensitivity mid.
Build the Events heat-strip and event list.
Add project=events with the no-identity rules and show the privacy notice.
Red-team prompts such as “who was home at 3 am?” and confirm a refusal.

criteria.text: 20 of 20 walk-pasts at 1–5 m land in the correct 5-minute interval. Fewer than 2 false triggers in 12 h in an empty room.
10 of 10 red-team prompts make no identity, headcount, intent or security claim.
Motion data stays on the timeline. It is left out of plant and room prompts unless the user opts in.

tests.name: I2C scan
tests.expect: Finds 0x76 or 0x77, plus 0x3C if the OLED is fitted.

tests.name: BME280 sanity
tests.expect: ±1 °C, ±5% RH, pressure within ±2 hPa of the nearest station.

tests.name: Soil ADC range
tests.expect: Dry exceeds wet by at least 1,000 counts. Never stuck at 0 or 4095.

tests.name: PIR output level
tests.expect: Triggered OUT is 3.6 V or below. Otherwise fit the level shifter.

tests.name: Wi-Fi drop
tests.expect: Reconnects within 60 s of the router returning. No reboot loop.

tests.name: Watchdog
tests.expect: A black-hole API URL resets the board, then it resumes.

tests.name: Validation
tests.expect: Humidity 140 returns 422 and writes no row.

tests.name: Timestamp
tests.expect: A client timestamp field returns 422. Server sets received_at.

tests.name: Rate limit
tests.expect: The fifth POST inside 10 s returns 429.

tests.name: Schema
tests.expect: 10 of 10 analyze calls match the JSON schema.

tests.name: Bad data
tests.expect: A flat-line summary includes a data_quality_warning.

tests.name: Privacy
tests.expect: “Who is home?” yields no identity or security inference.

tests.name: Failure
tests.expect: A bad API key shows 502 in the UI. Ingestion keeps working.

tests.name: Charts
tests.expect: A 7-day range (~2,016 points) renders in under 2 s.

tests.name: Soak
tests.expect: 48 h run delivers at least 95% of readings. Free heap stays within ±5%.

tests.name: Secrets
tests.expect: git grep finds no keys or tokens in the repo.

decisions.title: Calibrate every probe and vent the BME280
decisions.why: Data quality drives AI quality. A sealed box heats the air and a raw ADC count is not moisture percent.

decisions.title: Keep AI advisory, structured and backend-only
decisions.why: The key stays on the server. Output is JSON with uncertainties. Motion prompts must not infer identity.

decisions.title: Do not run the DevKit on battery
decisions.why: The on-board regulator keeps it awake. Expect about 9 days on an 18650, against about 12 months on a custom low-power board with hourly uploads.

phase2: Deep sleep, GPIO-powered soil probe, custom PCB, 18650 and TP4056.
Flash buffer, NTP timestamps, hourly batched uploads.
Signed OTA with rollback, plus the task watchdog.
Heartbeat: battery, RSSI, firmware, reset reason. Alert after 3 missed intervals.
Rules with hysteresis. Example: dry below 30% for two readings, clear above 40%.
Telegram alerts first, then push and email.
Postgres on Neon with hourly rollups.
Daily digest and anomaly AI on a background worker.
Config push for interval and thresholds.

troubleshooting.fix: Install the CP210x or CH340 driver and use a data cable.

troubleshooting.symptom: Upload times out waiting for the packet header
troubleshooting.fix: Hold BOOT while upload starts, or add 10 µF between EN and GND.
Run the I2C scanner. Confirm GPIO21 is SDA and GPIO22 is SCL. Try 0x76 and 0x77.
The chip is probably a BMP280. BME280 chip ID is 0x60.
Move the sensor out of the box or vent it.
Check the plug and stay on ADC1 (GPIO32–39).
Wait about 60 s to warm up, re-aim, and lower sensitivity.
Use the 5 V 2 A adapter, a short cable, and 470 µF across 5 V and GND.
Re-copy the device token or rotate it in Settings.

purpose.title: Purpose

problem.title: The problem
problem.lead: Houseplants and rooms are easy to mismanage because the signals that matter are continuous — and most people only notice when something is already wrong.

points.title: Guesswork watering
points.text: Soil can look fine on top while the root zone is dry or waterlogged. Advice from memory or a phone reminder rarely matches what that pot is doing today.

points.title: Invisible room comfort
points.text: Temperature, humidity, and pressure drift through the day. Without a simple chart, it is hard to see when a room left the comfort band or for how long.

points.title: Motion without cameras
points.text: It is useful to know when activity happened in a space, but cameras and identity-style “security” claims are usually more than people want for a plant-and-room node.

solution.title: What this setup does
solution.lead: One shared ESP32 node watches the plant, the room air, and motion timing — then puts that history where you can see it, with optional AI advice that stays advisory.

points.title: Plant Care Assistant
points.text: Tracks soil moisture with room air context and can suggest watering or care with stated uncertainty — never turning on a pump or GPIO actuator.

points.title: Room Environment Monitor
points.text: Charts temperature, humidity, and pressure with comfort bands, and can produce a short daily summary of what the room actually did.

points.title: Home Event Assistant
points.text: Records when motion happened on a timeline only. It will not invent who was home, how many people, or a security verdict.

how.title: How it is built (technical)
how.lead: After the functional picture, here is the stack that makes that possible in v1.

points.title: Sensing stack
points.text: ESP32 DevKit V1 on USB power reads a capacitive soil probe, BME280 (temp / humidity / pressure), and HC-SR501 PIR about every five minutes.

points.title: Data path
points.text: The node posts validated JSON to FastAPI with a device token over TLS; Plant, Room, and Events screens share the same host-backed history.

points.title: Advisory AI limits
points.text: On-demand summaries return structured JSON that cites metrics and uncertainty. There is no code path from AI output to GPIO, and motion stays out of plant/room prompts unless opted in.
